qc.label_under_test: A comeback in mutual labelling: in a passage whose earlier sentence introduces two people (My roommate and I clash constantly.), one labels the other (I see her as a slob) and the other labels the first back (and she sees me as a neat freak); it fires on the turned-back target and the word opening its label ('me', 'as', 'a'), with or without 'a'/'as'. Strongest when the narrator labelled first and is labelled back; weak without the lead-in sentence or when the narrator is the one answering back.

neighbours.label: A label handed back between two people: one person labels another (sees him as a tyrant, calls him a bore, considers him reckless) and then that other person labels the first in return (and he sees me as a slacker); it fires on the returned label's opening ('me', 'as', 'a', 'like'), friendly or hostile labels alike, with or without a sentence introducing the pair. A plain tit-for-tat with no label (I hate him and he hates me), a one-way label, or two people labelling the same third party stays quiet, and it is weak when the narrator is labelled first and answers back.
fire: I see my boss as a tyrant, and he sees me as a slacker.
She thinks of her brother as a genius, and he thinks of her as a saint.
I always called my roommate a bore, and he called me a nag.
My neighbor and I never got along: I considered him reckless, and he considered me uptight.
To me he was a hero, and to him I was a lucky fool.
I regard Tom as a mentor, and Tom regards me as a friend.
She treats him like a child, and he treats her like a drill sergeant.
I found the new coach arrogant, and he found me lazy.
quiet: I hate my boss, and he hates me.
I see my boss as a tyrant, and he rarely speaks to anyone at all.
She loves her brother, and he loves her just as much.
I always called my roommate a bore, and honestly I still do.
My neighbor and I never got along: we argued over the fence every single weekend.
I see the mayor as a fraud, and my uncle sees him as a fraud too.
She treats him kindly, and he treats her kindly in return.
I found the new coach arrogant, and so did the rest of the team.

predictions: most fire items above 0.20 (the 'to me he was a hero' and 'found me lazy' forms are the riskiest); near misses near zero
